lens: Flight-simulator cockpit: pre-flight briefing, in-call HUD, post-flight debrief with black-box replay
name: Flight Deck Cockpit
one_liner: A dark instrument-panel cockpit: every call gets a pre-flight briefing, a live HUD that coaches and scores each turn, and a black-box debrief you can replay.
lens_followed_or_changed: Followed the cockpit lens: pre-flight checklist, in-call HUD and black-box replay are core screens, sharing one grammar of gauges, status lamps and telemetry type. Changed three things. Research showed vendor UIs (Second Nature, Hyperbound, Mindtickle) are light and card-based, so a dark instrument UI stands apart, and a daylight mode keeps browsing readable. The lens says nothing about libraries, so the persona browser borrows faceted rails from Mobbin's WRITER and Lindy agent libraries. Chose shadcn/ui over HeroUI for owned code that contributors and Codex agents can edit. Self-scores if built as designed: A 8.5, B 8, C 8.5, D 6.5, E 6.5. Today's app falls short on D and E (no live coaching, three scenarios).

ui_stack.name: shadcn/ui on Base UI (MIT, copy-owned source)
ui_stack.role: Component layer: Dialog, Sheet, Tabs, Switch, Slider, Combobox, Toast, all as source inside the repo
ui_stack.why: Contributors and Codex agents can read and edit the components directly. Base UI became shadcn's default in July 2026; Radix and React Aria remain selectable. HeroUI (React Aria plus Tailwind v4, MCP server, llms.txt) is the runner-up if owned code is not wanted.

ui_stack.name: Motion (motion/react)

ui_stack.why: Declarative transitions with a reduced-motion path; keeps the HUD feeling alive without a custom animation engine.

ui_stack.name: TanStack Table

ui_stack.why: Headless sorting, filtering and faceting that pairs with shadcn table styling.

ui_stack.name: Recharts

ui_stack.name: Type stack: Sora, Inter, JetBrains Mono
ui_stack.role: Display headings, UI and transcript body, HUD numerals
ui_stack.why: Sora is already loaded for continuity; JetBrains Mono tabular-nums keep timers and scores from jittering.

palette.use: Cockpit background, dark default for flight and debrief
Instrument panels and cards on dark
Dividers, gauge tracks and card borders on dark
Secondary text and telemetry labels, about 6.7:1 on deck
Live and active state, primary action on dark, cue glow
Goal met or criterion on track
Watch items, heuristic-estimate lamp, pricing raised too early
Objection alerts and the End and grade control
Daylight background for landing, library, wizard, logbook, team
Primary action on light, AA contrast on white

design_language.typography: Sora 600-700 for headings and persona names; Inter 400-600 for UI and transcript body (16px minimum in live views); JetBrains Mono with tabular-nums for timers, gauge numerals and scores. Desktop base 15px, mobile 16px.
design_language.shape_and_depth: 8px panel radius, 12px for sheets and drawers. 1px hairline borders, no heavy shadows on dark; depth comes from a 1px inner top highlight. Only the live element gets a cyan glow. Tape gauges are 6px bars with segment ticks.
design_language.motion: Gauge tapes ease over 300ms; cue cards slide in from the right edge in 180ms and fade after 8 seconds; replay scrubbing is frame-accurate with requestAnimationFrame. prefers-reduced-motion swaps movement for opacity and freezes the orb.
design_language.iconography: lucide-react at 1.5px stroke, 16px inline and 20px in HUD rails. Custom SVG instrument glyphs (gauge, tape, status lamp, altimeter) carry the cockpit metaphor. No emoji in product UI.
design_language.theme_modes: Dark cockpit is default on /flight and /debrief; daylight on landing, library, wizard, logbook and team. A toggle in settings respects prefers-color-scheme. Both modes come from the same CSS variables on :root so contributors change one file. WCAG AA contrast for all text in both modes.

navigation_and_ia: Desktop: slim icon rail with Brief, Library, New persona, Logbook, Team, Contribute, Settings. Routes: /library, /library/[persona], /new (wizard), /brief/[scenario] (pre-flight), /flight/[id] (live HUD), /debrief/[id] (black box), /logbook, /team, /contribute. Mobile: bottom tab bar with Library, Fly, Logbook, More; Fly resumes the last pre-flight. Ctrl/Cmd+K opens the command palette to jump to any persona or start a flight. Keyboard: Space mutes, Enter sends, Esc opens the End and grade confirm.

live_coaching_and_scoring: Self-score D: 6.5 if the sidecar ships as designed. Architecture: the persona stays forbidden to coach. A separate grader call runs after each rep turn and returns rubric deltas plus at most one cue, rendered only to the rep. Cues come from fixed categories (objection, next question, talk-track phase, forbidden early claim such as price), each with evidence quotes and a Use line action. Gauges move per turn and the final grade uses the same rubric, so live numbers and the debrief agree. Throttle: one cue per 20 seconds, cues expire after 8 seconds, and a heuristic fallback shows an amber Estimate lamp rather than a silent score. In voice mode cues stay on screen only, so the audio channel stays clean.
persona_library_and_wizard: Self-score E: 6.5 if built as designed. Library: faceted browse across role, industry, difficulty, objection type and mode, seeded with a large open persona set. Each persona is a versioned JSON file validated by a zod schema in CI, so contributions arrive as reviewable PRs. Usage counts and 'flown N times' give social proof. Wizard: five steps (Source, Persona, Scenario, Rubric, Test flight). Source accepts a job description, product URL, CRM notes, an ICP or a pasted call. Generation uses OpenAI Structured Outputs against the same zod schema, streams fields into a preview with confidence chips, and never saves without a test flight. Export produces a PR-ready JSON file.
signature_moments: Pre-flight checklist: mic level, goal read and persona loaded each show a status lamp before Start flight enables.
Coach cue sheet: at most two cues on screen; Use line drops the suggested phrase into the input in one tap.
Black-box replay: scrub the call timeline and the rubric gauges rewind with it.
Evidence chips seek the replay to the exact second a quote was said.
Amber Estimate lamp when the grader falls back to heuristics, so a fallback score is never mistaken for a graded one.
Mobile long-press End and grade with a progress ring, so the call cannot end by accident.
openai_fund_angle: Show real OpenAI usage in the product, not just a logo. Each flight's report card lists the model behind each job: GPT-4.1-mini (default) for grading and coach cues, Structured Outputs for the wizard, and the Realtime API as a selectable voice engine beside ElevenLabs Agents, with a per-flight cost estimate. Settings lets a maintainer swap any slot to another OpenAI-compatible model. A /contribute page lists good-first personas and scenarios; the wizard drafts a persona JSON that passes the CI schema, then opens a prefilled GitHub PR for the contributor to submit (never auto-submitted). An AGENTS.md at the repo root tells Codex CLI how to run tests and add a persona. Codex fits maintainer work here: PR review of persona and rubric changes, release notes, and scorecard test fixtures.

implementation.migration_path: Phase 0, first PR: add Tailwind v4 and shadcn/ui on Base UI, map the old .card, .btn-primary and .input classes to shadcn variants, and ship the two token themes; no feature changes, so reviewers see only the token diff. Phase 1: persona JSON schema, seed library, library browse, wizard and Pre-flight screen. Phase 2: live HUD with the grader sidecar, cue throttle, heuristic fallback and mobile sheet, behind a flag until the live-call smoke test passes. Phase 3: black-box replay with wavesurfer for voice, logbook heatmap, manager view, and /contribute.

risks: Business viability: F1 as SaaS 4/10, crowded by funded rivals (Second Nature, Hyperbound, Mindtickle, Yoodli, Outdoo AI). F2 selling to entities 6/10: persona packs plus the scorecard engine licensed to training firms and call centres, with SCORM and LTI export as table stakes. F3 not worth building 3/10: worth building as open source, since OpenAI credits keep cost low.
Tailwind 3 to 4 migration touches every screen and the custom globals.css classes must be rewritten, so Phase 0 needs its own review.
Live coaching adds a per-turn grader call; if latency or cost is not budgeted, cues arrive after the moment has passed.
Dark cockpit can read as gimmicky or lose contrast; enforce WCAG AA on the token set and keep daylight mode as the browsing default.
Persona library quality is both the moat and the cost: a large set needs expert review, not just generation.
Sources disagree on Radix: shadcn says it stays fully supported, while one 2026 roundup says it is no longer maintained. Verify before choosing Base UI or Radix.
Process note: Mobbin reported high AI usage this month (about 895 credits used in this session) and said limits may require purchased credits once beta ends.
